name: Energy Bomber
doc: Energy Bomber (Adel's attack): the root, the main task and the sparks - an energy ball forming at the caster's bone, thrown, then hopping three times to the target with a two-point trail, a burst layout at the target with sparks flying off it, the screen flash, the sound; the damage. Its tasks are the port's code (FFNx mag217_energy_bomber.cpp) run on the program's memory (its pools and packet arenas in the magic buffer).

copy.doc: Where this effect's copy is in FF8_EN.exe: the program stands in for these functions.

module.doc: The port module whose code runs: its memory [from, + size) - in a copy, a block of its own.

exe_data.doc: The exe data the effect uses (@key in its values).

director.doc: The port's file loader, setup and root (they start its tasks)

parts.title: Director
parts.doc: The main task's timeline: the sound, the damage, its end; the screen flash rising and falling; the texture and the camera

parts.title: Energy ball
parts.doc: The ball layout forming at the caster's bone, thrown, then hopping three times to the target

parts.title: Trail
parts.doc: Two trail meshes behind the ball once it hops (their fade words are never read: the renderer's draw mode 0x30 has no fade)

parts.title: Burst
parts.doc: The burst layout at the target

parts.title: Sparks
parts.doc: Sparks flying off the target from the burst's first ticks, slowing

groups.label: Screen flash
groups.doc: Its level, rising over the first ticks, falling over the last ones

params.label: Sound
params.doc: At the main task's sound tick

params.label: Sound tick
params.doc: The sound at this tick of the main task

params.label: Damage tick
params.doc: The damage at this tick of the main task

params.label: End tick
params.doc: The main task's last tick (the screen flash falls toward it; sparks still alive then are dropped)

params.label: Level
params.doc: The screen flash's level (4096 = full white)

params.label: Rise ticks
params.doc: It rises over the main task's first ticks (at least 1)

params.label: Fall ticks
params.doc: It falls over its last ticks, to 0 at the end tick (at least 1)

params.label: Texture file
params.doc: The texture file its loader reads from the magic folder (a name of at most 31 letters)

params.label: Camera track
params.doc: The camera track its setup plays (any length: its offsets are its own)

params.label: Bone
params.doc: The caster's bone the ball forms at

params.label: Lift
params.doc: The ball this much above the bone (y up)

params.label: Throw tick
params.doc: The ball follows the bone until this tick, then flies on along its last step

params.label: Hop tick
params.doc: From this tick three eased hops of 4 ticks each to the target (the trail from then)

params.label: Hop height
params.doc: The first hop's point this high above the target

params.label: Hop spread
params.doc: The first hop's point: a random x up to this either side of the target (the second hop mirrors it; at least 1)

params.label: Ball
params.doc: The prim-model layout of the ball (its models' animation)

params.label: Trail model
params.doc: The prim model of each trail point (a mesh: an edited one keeps its vertices)

params.label: Tick
params.doc: The burst starts at this tick of the main task, at the target

params.label: Ticks
params.doc: It plays this many ticks

params.label: Burst
params.doc: The prim-model layout of the burst (its models' animation)

params.label: Spawn ticks
params.doc: Sparks spawn at the burst's ticks 1 to this

params.label: A tick
params.doc: How many a tick (64 at most alive; at least 1)

params.label: Speed
params.doc: A spark's speed: this + a random below the next, in a random direction

params.label: Speed random
params.doc: (at least 1)

params.label: Drag
params.doc: Each tick its first speed / 2^this is taken off (4: 1/16)

params.label: Life
params.doc: A spark's ticks (its flipbook frame = its tick)

params.label: Size
params.doc: Its sprite's size

params.label: Depth
params.doc: Its sprite's depth offset (negative = nearer)

params.label: Spark
params.doc: The sprite sequence spark (a flipbook: an edited one keeps as many frames)
